summary: The exact candidate lacks the described successor admission fixes. Its 49 existing language tests pass, but independent probes reproduce bounds substitution, validation after authentication, forbidden runtime-object normalization, and source-profile conformance errors. No accepted-Complete or cryptographic bypass is claimed.

findings.title: Public entry points admit unregistered bounds under the frozen profile
findings.observed: Bounds admission checks registry/profile labels but does not require the exact registered 8861 bytes. Raising instructionsPerEntrypoint and localsPerEntrypoint from 64 to 65 admits a 65-let action rejected by the pinned bounds. createSimulator then returns Simulation with executedInstructions='65'. Appending one whitespace byte to bounds also compiles and produces another boundsHash under the same registry/profile.
findings.required_correction: Register and enforce the exact frozen bounds bytes across public parse/check/elaborate/compile, simulator, derivation and mapping admission. Keep custom limits exclusively in explicitly NONADMITTED internal helpers. Add positive pinned-byte and negative changed-byte/raised-limit tests.

findings.title: Backend authentication runs before source and runtime admission
findings.observed: An invalid backend source invokes authenticate once before returning stage-8 PROGRAM_ENCODING. With the pinned loan source/bounds, an input containing an extra field invokes authenticate once before returning stage-9 INPUT_SCHEMA. Neither probe reaches commit.
findings.required_correction: Complete source/bounds/BoundProgram correspondence and inert closed runtime-schema/bounds admission before invoking authenticate. Authenticate an immutable admitted tuple, then perform authenticated checks, derivation and the deployment-owned verification/commit interface. Add callback-count negative controls requiring zero authentication calls for inadmissible inputs.

findings.title: Cloning bypasses forbidden runtime-object checks
findings.observed: Using the pinned loan example, inputs with a hidden unknown property, symbol property, custom prototype, or enumerable action getter all return Simulation. The getter executes once. canonicalEncode rejects these original objects, but structuredClone removes forbidden properties/prototypes or evaluates accessors before validation examines the clone.
findings.required_correction: Validate and snapshot original runtime objects through a bounded descriptor-based inert-data admission routine before cloning or reading accessors. Reject forbidden properties and prototypes without invoking getters. Cover both derive/simulate and evaluate with regression probes.

findings.title: Valid policies following their target action are rejected
findings.observed: A valid rounding-none policy targeting write(run,cash) produces TypedProgram when placed before run, but NAME_RESOLUTION when placed after run. The frozen semantics explicitly permits policies before or after their actions and resolves action/local metadata over the complete action table.
findings.required_correction: Remove the policy-before-action restriction from both validation and lowering. Preserve declaration-before-use for the policy unit and required rounding-local relationships. Test valid policies in both positions and invalid metadata references.

findings.title: Closed diagnostic priority and source-map classification are not preserved
findings.observed: A source with duplicate unit declarations returns stage-4 DUPLICATE_NAME with pinned bounds, but stage-8 PROGRAM_ENCODING with '{}', masking the earlier source error. Separately, altering a Core sourceRef span and recomputing programHash returns PROGRAM_ENCODING instead of the required SOURCE_MAP.
findings.required_correction: Preserve source-stage priority while enforcing registered bounds, and distinguish deterministic source-map/Core correspondence failures from other program-encoding failures. Add mixed-stage and source-map-specific diagnostic tests.
